analysis:
The PR turns SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator from a strict per-path FIFO mutex into a shared/exclusive lease with FIFO fairness, plus tryUpgrade/downgrade. Stage reads (SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Read.swift:126-129 and 201-204) now take .shared leases. The default for makeAccess stays .exclusive, so writers, scans, tryAcquire maintenance and retirement keep exclusive access. Related threats: T-041 (the encrypted SSD prefix cache, A-001) and T-016/T-029 for availability.

I traced the head coordinator logic (SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift:119-220).
- admits() lets a shared request in unless the first holder is exclusive, and lets an exclusive request in only when there are no holders.
- enqueue() admits immediately only when the waiter queue is empty. A queued exclusive request therefore blocks later shared requests, so writers are not starved by a stream of readers.
- cancel() of a waiter removes it and re-admits queued shared requests behind it.
- release() removes the access from holders and admits waiters under the lock. Continuations are resumed outside the lock.
- tryUpgrade() requires the caller to be the sole holder with an empty queue. downgrade() admits queued shared requests.
- tryAcquire() still requires a fully untracked path, so maintenance and eviction skip any file with an active reader. That is conservative.
- The state machine is consistent: the .active, .waiting and .finished transitions are guarded by the lock, and acquire()'s catch path calls release(), which is a no-op unless the access is active.

I found no confidentiality, integrity or authorization regression. The on-disk format, crypto, HMAC names, TTL and epoch handling are untouched.

Unverified contracts, because the code is not in the supplied evidence:
(1) the writer or duplicate-validation caller that uses tryUpgrade/downgrade, and whether file replacement or mutation can happen under a shared lease;
(2) SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove's handling of the new unusedSince parameter, which is plumbed through retireOwnedEntries/retireIndexedEntries (+Maintenance.swift:29-39), and its callers, which could affect TTL/LRU purge guarantees for T-041;
(3) the readAttempt acquire path, which the shown code does not include.
The next pass should check these.
